questions.question: Two sphere of mass m and M are situated in air and the gravitational force between them is F . The space around the masses is now filled with a liquid of specific gravity 3 . The gravitational force will now be
questions.explanation: Gravitational force does not depend on the surrounding medium—unlike electrostatic or buoyant forces. Hence, filling the space with liquid of any density leaves the mutual gravitational pull unchanged.

questions.question: If the mass of one particle is increased by 50 \% and the mass of another particle is decreased by 50 \% , the force between them: (keeping the distance same)
questions.explanation: Let the initial masses be m1m_1 and m2m_2. The initial force FinitialF_{{initial}} is Finitial  ∝  m1 m2. F_{{initial}} \;\; m_1\,m_2. One mass is increased by 50%, so it becomes 1.5 m11.5\,m_1. The other mass is decreased by 50%, so it becomes 0.5 m20.5\,m_2. The new product of masses is (1.5 m1) (0.5 m2)=0.75 (m1 m2). (1.5\,m_1)\,(0.5\,m_2) = 0.75\,(m_1\,m_2). Thus, the new force is 0.750.75 times the original force, i.e.\ it is reduced to 75% of its old value. Hence, the force decreases by 25%.
